title: Libertarian Party May 22-26 Convention in Denver: A Major Opportunity for Anti-Prohibitionists to Make Ourselves Heard by National Media In Cannabis Friendly City.

content_html_sanitized:
Analysis by Richard Cowan 

The Libertarian Party’s 2008 National Convention in Denver, May 22ndthrough the 26th, will be a major opportunity for marijuana law reformers as well as the broader anti-Drug War movement to get national media attention. 

Unlike the two “major” party conventions, which will be scripted to the Establishment’s prohibitionist party line on the inside, and a zoo of all sorts of protestors on the outside, the LP will be entirely open to us and we will have very little competition for media attention. 

Libertarians are fundamentally opposed to the Drug War, so there will be no duck and run maneuvers like Obama’s flip-flop on decrim. 

See 

Obama Flip-Flops On Decrim. Shame on Him, Or Shame on Us? Why Do Politicians Fear Something A Huge Majority Supports? Who Is Their Real Constituency? 

On the other hand, if we don’t show up, the degree of LP’s focus on the Drug War will depend solely on the success of Steve Kubby’s bid for the LP’s Presidential nomination. 

While Steve’s prospects look good now, there is talk that “former” Drug Warrior, and former Republican Congressman, Bob Barr may seek the LP nomination. 

See 

Paranoia and the Party Line on Medical Marijuana. Who Do They Think They Are Fooling? The DEA and Bob Barr. 

Barr claims to have converted, and the Lord loves repentant sinners, and the media really do love a story with an angle. Consequently, Barr will definitely get a lot of attention, if he does run. We just need to be sure that he really has converted, and that the focus remains 

on OUR issue. I have no idea how he will be received by the Libertarian Party rank and file, but it is clear that he intends to try and pick up where Ron Paul left off. (The money-bomb squad?) 

Obviously, I hope that a large anti-Drug War, pro-medical marijuana turnout helps Steve Kubby’s candidacy, and it is important to note that almost anyone who joins the LP and shows up in Denver can probably vote at the convention. (They are still free to vote however they please in November.) 

Also, having a medical marijuana patient as the LP candidate will make it more difficult for the mainstream media and the Progressive blogoshpere to ignore us. 

See

Sicko and The Return of MarijuanaNews.com. The Failure of the Left to Address the Drug War. By Richard Cowan. 

But there are plenty of other reasons for us to be there in numbers. 

First, the Democratic National Convention is also being held in Denver from August 25thto the 28th, and if we get enough publicity in May, it may help remind everyone about our issues in the midst of the Democrats’ cacophony. 

Second, Denver is home to one of the most successful grass roots marijuana reform movements in the country, Mason Tvert’s Safer Alternative for Enjoyable Recreation, and we can show the local media that he has national support. 

See 

The Strategy of Comparing Risks of Cannabis and Alcohol. When an Old Argument Catches On. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

and 

Denver, Host City of 2008 Democratic Convention, Votes for De Facto ‘Decrim’. Richard Cowan Comments on Presidential Candidates on NORML Podcast. 

and 

Program notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report for April 21, 2005. Sativex Maker Declares War on Sick and Dying. Students Lead Drugwar Resistance Against Police. 420 A Huge Success In Colorado. 

Third, Colorado has a medical marijuana law that is protecting a number of patients. It would be very helpful to them to have the issue reinforced by having a medical marijuana patient on the LP ticket. 

See 

Annotated NORML Weekly News for December 6, 2007 – The Drug War Is Racist; Colorado and California police Have to Follow State NOT Federal Laws; Hemp Still Scares Narks. 

I will be writing more about this soon, and Steve and I will be talking about it on the Steve Kubby Show on BlogTalkRadio.com on Monday morning. Stay tuned.
